Tier 1 features: document regime, facility bans partially. Severity: no imprisonment for being trans nationally; arrest possible in some states (trespass). Severity ladder: 2-3 mostly. Score maybe 0.35-0.45. Given passport regime = universal exposure, facility bans in many states, custody abuse documented, hostile official climate but functioning courts with some relief... Border/document exposure is universal though. I'd say around 0.40-0.45. The visa cable instructing refusal is traveler-facing. Detentions of foreign citizens over visa issues led allied advisories. Severity is moderate — refusal of entry, facility exclusion, occasional arrest. Not imprisonment generally. I'll go 0.42.

No LGR (resident gap — not traveler exposure unless documents doubted; dossier says "a visitor whose passport marker differs from presentation should expect no local precedent for documentary flexibility" — an open question, not documented exposure). Very thin dossier — no violence, no border rules, no facilities. Extrapolate: criminalization removed, diplomatic statements supportive, but no protections and thin record. Dossier 2 has documented tolerance (LGB) and protective diplomacy; dossier 4 has decriminalization + joint statement but no attitude data. Dossier 4 has constitutional marriage ban (resident/LGB) and no anti-discrimination. I'd put dossier 4 slightly below dossier 2: ~0.65-0.68. Dossier 2: 0.70. Dossier 4: 0.66.

Hmm, but dossier 4 is thinner. Rule 13 says thin data shouldn't default to midpoint; extrapolate. Structural: no criminalisation, no documented targeting, no documented acceptance. Neutral-ish governance. I'd say 0.65.

Article 193 criminalizes sex between men (7 years) — enforced. Public morality strictly enforced. Dress-code policing continued post-ruling. 2017 arrest of personality for looking too feminine (2 weeks detention). No LGBTQ association, media censorship, film bans, gender segregation. Foreign HIV+ deported. Entry testing proposal disavowed. No criminalization of trans presentation now (struck down 2022) but sodomy law enforced and applies to trans people read as same-sex relationships; official discrimination persists. Tier: state-tolerated hostility with thin recourse; some ongoing dress policing (undated scale). Severity: up to 7 years under Article 193 if read as same-sex relation; detention risk. The cross-dressing ban is struck down — so the primary presentation offence is gone, but enforcement legacy persists and officials discriminate. Score maybe 0.30-0.40. Compare anchor 0.35-C (police extortion of visibly trans) and 0.45-A (facility bans). Dossier 5: enforced sodomy law + ongoing official discrimination + no recourse + no association + censorship, but no documented current presentation arrests post-2022. Rule 2: sexuality law as police lever against gender-nonconforming — documented "public morality laws strictly enforced, prosecutions of LGBTQ people documented", officials discriminate against trans people (2023). That's a lever. I'd say 0.33-0.38. Let's say 0.35.

Actually consider: is dossier 5 worse than dossier 1? Dossier 1 has universal document exposure and facility bans; dossier 5 has enforced sodomy law + official discrimination but struck-down presentation offence. Dossier 1's severity: entry refusal, facility exclusion, arrest in some states, prison conversion therapy (for those in custody). Dossier 5: arrest possibility under morality laws if read as same-sex; official hostility; detention 2 weeks happened in 2017. I think dossier 5 slightly below or comparable to dossier 1. Precedence ladder: dossier 1 tier 1 (document/facility universal exposure) with no working remedy nationally (litigation pending, some states). Dossier 5 tier 2-ish (state-tolerated targeting via morality enforcement + official discrimination). Hmm, dossier 5's presentation offence struck down — so what's the universal exposure? Official discrimination, dress policing legacy, morality law applied to relationships. Gender segregation means visitor-facing: segregated spaces. That's an everyday exposure.

I'd put dossier 5 at 0.33, dossier 1 at 0.42. Actually is dossier 1 higher? Dossier 1: no criminalization of trans identity, functioning courts partially blocking orders, hate crime statute, employment protection, half of states no bans. But universal passport/visa exposure with documented detentions and foreign advisories. 0.42 seems right — near 0.45-A but with added document regime and custody abuse; but also with more protections. Let's say 0.40.

1: 0.40
